clue.text: Sheep Bill's got into position

indicators.note: Bill's has got into, so the bill's letters go inside the word for position

parts.note: a position is a job
a bill is an account, abbreviated AC

explanation.surface: A man called Bill has landed himself a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill's got into' is read as 'Bill has got into', so 's is not a possessive. Jacob is a piebald breed of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob is a breed of spotted, often many-horned sheep.

clue.text: Yellow featured in one game or another

indicators.note: featured in says the colour's letters appear inside the other game

parts.note: another game here is jacks, played by tossing small metal pieces
straw is a pale yellow colour

explanation.surface: A yellow piece appears in one board game or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the second game, jacks (also called knucklebones), and 'one game' is the definition: jackstraws, also called pick-up sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackstraws is a game of picking up thin sticks from a heap without moving the others.

clue.text: Billy may …

definitions.meaning: a billy is a camping pot for boiling water, a billycan
may in the sense of being permitted to

explanation.surface: Billy may, the clue running on into the next two.
explanation.definitionFit: A billy is a metal cooking tin, and may means is allowed to, both matching the word.

clue.text: … perhaps favour …

definitions.meaning: an archaic adverb meaning probably or perhaps
to favour a parent is to resemble them

explanation.surface: Continues the run of clues: Billy may perhaps favour one.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it means resemble; as one it is an old word for perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Belike is archaic for probably, and to favour someone in looks is to resemble them.

clue.text: Deplorable, the French record

parts.note: in British slang chronic means very bad, deplorable
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs that a record by the French is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: CHRONIC in informal British English means awful or of very poor quality, not just long-lasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a written historical account, a record of events in order.

clue.text: … one blooming engineer, miles away from explosive device

parts.note: CE, civil engineer, is a crossword engineer

indicators.note: away from says the letter for miles is removed from the device

parts.note: a landmine is a buried explosive device

explanation.surface: An engineer flowers once safely miles away from a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' takes M out of the device. 'one blooming' looks like a mild British swear word but means a plant that flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The celandine is a yellow-flowered plant, so one that blooms.

clue.text: Try to bring up good-for-nothing, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a wretch is a worthless, despicable person

explanation.surface: A parent tries to raise a ne'er-do-well child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring up' looks like raising a child, but it means vomit. WRETCH and RETCH sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to strain to vomit, trying to bring up the stomach contents.

clue.text: Several days knight finished without honour

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for finished encloses the honour

parts.note: over means finished
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A knight spends several days finished without being decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' has its old sense of outside here, not lacking. A month is 'several days' (thirty of them).
explanation.definitionFit: This month has thirty days, so it is several days taken together.

clue.text: Merciful release from cage rude cop arranged

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the three words are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner is released from a cage by a rude policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup de grâce is a death blow that ends suffering, a merciful release.

clue.text: To some extent, the choicest nymph

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nymph is described as somewhat the finest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Echo was a mountain nymph who could only repeat others' words.

clue.text: With dim illumination, clubs mistakenly let lad in

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: mistakenly says the following words are put together wrongly, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bouncers at nightclubs wrongly admit a youngster in the gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests nightclubs and bouncers, but it is the card suit. 'mistakenly' rearranges the three words after it, and 'in' is part of what gets rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A room lit by candles has soft, dim illumination.

clue.text: Pained expression after initially viewing warrant

indicators.note: after puts the pained cry behind the initial letter
initially says take just the first letter of viewing

parts.note: ouch is what one says when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone winces on first seeing a warrant served on them.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text has a stray 0 that the printed page lacks. 'initially' gives V from viewing, and 'after' puts OUCH behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To warrant something is to guarantee or vouch for it, as verbs.

clue.text: Reactionary in charge of family leading them into breeding establishment

indicators.note: into says the run of letters is placed inside the breeding establishment's word

parts.note: a stud is a farm where animals are bred

indicators.note: leading means coming before the word them in the run

parts.note: kin means family or relatives
taken as written

explanation.surface: A conservative patriarch steers the family toward a horse-breeding farm.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text has a stray 0 the page lacks. IC + KIN, 'leading' THEM, goes 'into' STUD: ST-ICKINTHEM-UD.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick-in-the-mud resists change, so is a reactionary in the loose sense of an old fogey.

clue.text: One residence I can put together is worth a fortune

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a nest is a home or residence
I can is the same as I'm able

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they can assemble a priceless home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I can' becomes I'M ABLE, so IMABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inestimable means too valuable to be measured, so worth a fortune.

clue.text: Roger's a lot to chew over — he's a stargazer

indicators.note: to chew over suggests grinding up, so the letters of the words are rearranged

parts.note: taken with its S
taken as written

explanation.surface: Roger has plenty to ponder, being an observer of the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of Roger's is part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrologer studies the stars and planets, so is a stargazer.

clue.text: Whirl around and grin back

indicators.note: back says the word for grin is read from end to start

parts.note: a leer is a sly or lascivious grin

explanation.surface: Someone spins round and smirks over their shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to spin or whirl round dizzily.

clue.text: Divine entering distances for way back

indicators.note: entering says the divine's letters go inside the word for distances

parts.note: mileages are distances measured in miles
DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a divine or theologian

explanation.surface: A holy man walks long distances to find the way home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective but is a noun: a clergyman, abbreviated DD (Doctor of Divinity).
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval period lies far in the past, so it is an era from way back.

clue.text: Cockney Eliza put on nothing petite

parts.note: to do a show is to put it on
O is the zero shape for nothing
petite means little

explanation.surface: A cockney flower girl puts on nothing at all, being so small.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle is the cockney flower seller in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza Doolittle is Shaw's cockney flower girl, so the surname identifies her.

clue.text: Jump to conclusions; before jump is half over, magistrate drops round

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: half over says only the first half of jump remains
drops says the round letter is let go from the magistrate

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A judge decides early, before a jump is half finished.
explanation.walkthrough: JU is half of jump; DOGE (Venice's chief magistrate) drops O to give DGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To prejudge is to decide before the evidence is in, jumping to conclusions.

clue.text: Fruit women alter drastically

indicators.note: drastically suggests a radical change, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Women radically change their diet to fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A watermelon is a large juicy fruit with green rind and red flesh.

clue.text: Just fine

definitions.meaning: just means equitable, treating all equally
fine means acceptable or pleasant, as weather that is dry

explanation.surface: Fair enough, just about fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means just or equitable, and also fine, as of weather or moderately good.

clue.text: Untidy chap has to scrape round bottom of jar

indicators.note: round says the scraping word goes about the letter

parts.note: to scuff is to scrape or graze

indicators.note: bottom of says take the final letter of jar, the bottom in a down clue

explanation.surface: A slob has to scrape out the bottom of a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom of' gives R, the last letter of jar, and SCUFF goes 'round' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruff is an informal British word for a scruffy, unkempt person.

clue.text: Important, grinding millet — crush extremely for Aussie bird

parts.note: major means important

indicators.note: grinding breaks up the grain, so the letters of millet with the pair are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: extremely says take the first and last letters of crush

explanation.surface: An Australian bird is busy crushing grain for its feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives CH, the first and last letters of crush, which join MILLET in the shuffle to make MITCHELL. The Major Mitchell is a pink cockatoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Major Mitchell's cockatoo is a pink and white cockatoo native to Australia.

clue.text: The necessary pachyderm…

definitions.meaning: old British slang for money, the wherewithal
a thick-skinned animal such as an elephant or rhinoceros

explanation.surface: The necessary thick-skinned beast, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: RHINO is dated British slang for money, just as 'the necessary' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old slang for cash, and also short for the thick-skinned rhinoceros.

clue.text: … is employed to bear two kings and a weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue a word bearing others holds them up from below, so it comes after

parts.note: K and R, the chess abbreviation and Rex, both stand for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heavy beast is used to carry two kings and a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: IS 'bears' (supports from below) KR in the down light. A kris is a Malay dagger with a wavy blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay or Indonesian dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: Zealous artist given an offer

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist
a bid is an offer, as at an auction

explanation.surface: An eager painter is handed an offer for their work.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid in the figurative sense means fanatical or extremely zealous.

clue.text: Home with basket case for noise that's disturbing

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: case for says the basket's letters enclose the noise

parts.note: a trug is a shallow garden basket
din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A deranged person at home makes a disturbing racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'basket case' looks like a phrase for a madman, but the basket (TRUG) is the case holding DIN. A trug is a British gardener's basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Intruding means encroaching unwelcome, which is disturbing others.

clue.text: Dark liquid — I've never known its origins

indicators.note: its origins says take the first letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: Someone admits they never learned where a dark fluid came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink is a coloured fluid, usually dark, used for writing.

clue.text: Eats out, entertaining surgeon (retired) and docker

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the assembled letters are read backwards
entertaining means holding, so the surgeon's letters go inside

parts.note: to erode is to eat away or eat out
a vet is an animal surgeon

explanation.surface: A dockworker dines out with a retired surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make 'retired' look like it applies to the surgeon alone, but it turns the whole container backwards; that gives SEDORE around TEV.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships, a docker or longshoreman.

clue.text: Ascetic putting potassium in 19

indicators.note: in says the element symbol is placed inside the word

parts.note: refers to the answer at 19 across
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A holy man treats himself with a potassium supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: A fakir is a Muslim or Hindu religious ascetic living on alms.
